claim.markdown_says: The page appears to be blank except for the watermark/footer text at the bottom. Since you've instructed me to ignore watermark text, and there is no other visible content on this page, there is no text to extract.
claim.why_it_matters: Transcription-tool meta-text left in the spec file. The substance of the observation is correct — page 1260 really is blank — so no normative content is lost here and this is not a content defect. But it is first-person conversational residue ('you've instructed me...') sitting inside what is supposed to be the standard's text, and it is exactly the marker of the summarised-not-transcribed failure mode. It should be swept out on sight, both because it pollutes full-text search of the spec and because leaving one instance in place makes the class harder to grep for on pages where the same tool DID replace real content with a description.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed on both sides; the claim misquotes neither source. PDF side: rendered specs/ISO_COBOL PDF page 1260 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1260/spec_p1260.png, 2550x3300). Visual inspection shows a wholly empty page carrying only the single license footer line '[per-copy licence stamp]' I did not rely on my eye alone: a pixel scan of the region above the footer (y=0..3000, sampled every 2px in both axes) returned 0 pixels below gray 200 with a minimum gray value of 255 — i.e. mathematically pure white, no faint ink, no rule, no figure. The footer band (y=3000..3300) returned 5171 dark pixels, accounting for the footer text alone. The page-workunit tool independently reported '0 with figure content'. Page 1260 is genuinely blank apart from the licensing watermark. Markdown side: the quoted sentence is present verbatim in the canonical transcription at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 53186, immediately under the ' / ## Page [1260](#page-1260)' heading (lines 53183-53184) and immediately before the page-1261 heading (line 53188). The preceding lines are the tail of the index ('Zero-length literal / Definition [107]'), so the residue sits in the spec body between two page anchors where a reader or a full-text search would take it for standard text. This is not page-break furniture, line wrapping, hyphenation, or a formatting artifact: it is a paragraph of first-person English prose that exists nowhere in the source document, inserted into the transcription. So the difference between the two artifacts is real and verifiable: the PDF page contains no prose; the markdown contains 43 words of conversational tool output. The claim is accurate as to both what the PDF shows and what the markdown says, and its own characterization is honest — it explicitly concedes that no normative content is lost. I find nothing to refute.
verdict.corrected_description:
Real, but the label and severity overstate it, and one supporting rationale does not survive checking.

(1) Severity should be cosmetic / transcription-hygiene, not structural. Page 1260 of the PDF carries zero normative content (verified: 0 non-white pixels above the footer). Nothing was lost, displaced, or garbled; no rule, syntax diagram, general format, or index entry is affected. The transcription's factual assertion is correct. The defect is purely that non-source prose was inserted into the spec body.

(2) The kind 'summarised-not-transcribed' is a misnomer for this instance. Nothing was summarised in place of content, because there was no content to summarise. The accurate characterization is 'transcription-tool meta-text emitted for a genuinely blank page' — a first-person artifact of the extraction session ('Since you've instructed me to ignore watermark text...') rather than a substitution of description for substance. It resembles the summarised-not-transcribed failure mode without being an instance of it.

(3) The claim's argument that leaving this in place 'makes the class harder to grep for on pages where the same tool DID replace real content with a description' is not supported by the file. I swept the entire 2.9 MB specs/ISO_COBOL.md for the full family of conversational-residue markers — "you've/you have instructed|asked|told me", "as an/your AI", "I cannot/can't/am unable to extract|transcribe|read", "there is no text/content to extract|transcribe", "appears to be blank", "no other visible content", "I'll transcribe|extract", "Since you" — and line 53186 is the sole hit in the whole document. There is no broader class hiding behind it; this is an isolated instance, not the visible tip of a pattern.

Correct remediation: delete line 53186 outright, leaving the page-1260 anchor and heading with an empty body (matching how other blank pages are represented), or replace it with a neutral marker such as '*(page intentionally blank)*'. No spec content needs to be recovered from the PDF.
